messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 tail latency spike detected for router service in eu-west-2. 10:03 UTC. Severity: high. Automated paging initiated.

oncall-maria: i'm on it — joining bridge. can someone paste the current p95/p99 numbers?

jordan_telemetry: p95 ~ 220ms baseline -> 520ms now. p99 baseline 1.2s -> 6.8s currently. streaming stall rate up ~8% (was <0.5%).

lee_sre: seeing a big increase in long tail for streaming sessions, looks correlated with a routing weight shift to shard-42 in euw2. heatmap shows shard-42 QPS doubled.

sam_platform: pulling router policy diff from last rollout... gives me a sec.

ops-bot: livebridge created: https://redwood/bridges/BR-4123456799 (auto) — channel #incidents bridge -> join to coordinate.

oncall-maria: joined bridge. tagging tai_netinfra and lee_sre. cs-ana please assemble customer impact blurb.

cs-ana: preliminary: ~12% of streaming customers in euw2 saw stalls >5s in last 10m. no 5xx spike yet but degraded UX for chat streaming. major customers: AcmeCorp, Boxrides. notifying AE.

lee_sre: allocating some logs: router tail traces show a misassignment loop where loadsplit policy favored the hot shard repeatedly. snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:01:22Z router[shard-42]: weight_update: policy=loadsplit v=3 -> applied weight 0.62
2026-03-15T10:01:23Z router[shard-17]: egress: eviction_count=0 -> redirected to shard-42
2026-03-15T10:01:23Z router[shard-42]: queue_len=2048 latency=4.2s
```

lee_sre: looks like the recent policy rollout increased eager fallback threshold which caused small zones to route to shard-42 even when capacity was saturated.

sam_platform: i have the rollout ID: rollout-2026-03-15-09:59 (loadsplit v3). we can roll back that rollout. is that safe?

oncall-maria: prioritize mitigation with minimal blast radius: 1) scale up dedicated workers for shard-42 2) revert loadsplit weights -> previous commit 7f3a9 3) temporarily lower eager-fallback threshold to prefer local. pick one, coordinate.

tai_netinfra: scaling on the pool: issuing scale +6 GPUs to euw2-router-pool now. ETA ~3m.

ops-bot: exec: kubectl scale deployment router-euw2 --replicas=18 --namespace=prod
ops-bot: command completed: request accepted.

jordan_telemetry: after scale request: p95 -> 310ms, p99 -> 2.1s (improving). streaming stall rate down to 3.1%.

oncall-maria: good. still high but trending. let's queue rollback on the routing policy as step 2. sam, please prepare the revert and a canary check.

sam_platform: preparing revert: running git revert on infra-config repo. applying to canary region first (euw1). will patch euw2 after canary looks ok.

sam_platform: canary applied to euw1. monitoring canary metrics...

jordan_telemetry: canary p99 unchanged in euw1 (as expected, low traffic), no regressions. approving roll forward to euw2.

sam_platform: applied revert to euw2 routing policy. rollout status: 83% -> 100% applied.

lee_sre: immediate difference in router traces: shard-42 weight dropped from 0.62 -> 0.18, redistributed across shards-12/17/28. queue_len for shard-42 down to ~120.

jordan_telemetry: metrics: p95 -> 240ms, p99 -> 1.05s, streaming stall rate -> 0.6% (close to baseline).

cs-ana: customer impact update: AcmeCorp noticed ~14% degrade window between 10:00-10:16 UTC; CS notified; they accepted workaround (client-side reconnect backoff) while we mitigated.

oncall-maria: nice job. timeline for RCA and follow-ups: we should capture why eager-fallback thresholds were bumped in v3 — was it intentional? sam, can you link the rollout PR?

sam_platform: PR: https://git.redwood/r/routing/pulls/4521 — description mentioned performance optimization for cold shards but tests didn't cover skewed zone scenarios.

lee_sre: root cause hypothesis: loadsplit v3 included an aggressive eager-fallback delta that was benign under even load tests but caused a positive feedback loop (hot shard attracted >50% of fallback traffic) under real skew. action items: add heatmap-based gating to rollout, extend canary to include a simulated hot-shard scenario, and add an automatic throttle when a shard queue_len crosses 1500.

oncall-maria: ok. create postmortem tracker and assign owners. i'll draft immediate blameless postmortem and notify PM/product.

ops-bot: action created: INCIDENT-4123456799 in tracker. assignees: lee_sre (RCA), sam_platform (fix + rollout guard), jordan_telemetry (alert tuning), cs-ana (customer comms).

oncall-maria: closing the live bridge in 10m if metrics remain stable. thanks all — follow-ups in INCIDENT-4123456799.

jordan_telemetry: last check (10:50 UTC): p95 225ms, p99 350ms, streaming stalls 0.4% — stable.

oncall-maria: closing bridge. final note for postmortem: impact window 10:00-10:20 UTC, ~12% of euw2 streaming sessions experienced stalls >5s, mitigated by scale + rollback. next steps: rollout guard, alert threshold tweak (p99 > 2s), postmortem writeup due EOD. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: BRIDGE CLOSED: https://redwood/bridges/BR-4123456799.
